name: Dielectric Manufacturing Iowa
old_description: Milwaukee-Area Contract Manufacturer of Precision Plastic and Metal Parts and Components, With Value-Added Services
about:
Dielectric Manufacturing operates from a 100,000-square-foot headquarters in Richfield, Wisconsin, just northwest of Milwaukee, with additional production plants in Waupaca, Wisconsin; Lake Mills, Iowa; and Richmond, Illinois. The company traces its roots to 1966 when Ray Esser founded Dielectric Corporation in central Wisconsin. The Esser family retains private ownership, and the name was updated to Dielectric Manufacturing in 2019 to reflect expanded capabilities beyond plastics into metal machining and carbon fiber composites.

The firm functions as a single-source contract manufacturer, handling design collaboration, prototyping, machining, fabrication, welding, finishing, assembly, kitting, packaging, and inventory management. Its equipment roster includes vertical and horizontal machining centers, 5-axis milling, 6-axis laser cutting, routing, stamping, turning, bending, cold forming, and plastic and metal welding. The Richfield facility opened in 2020; the Waupaca site specializes in ferrous metals, while the Richmond location, acquired in October 2025 as EMS Industrial & Service Co., produces busbars. All three Wisconsin and Iowa plants hold ISO 9001:2015 certification, and the Waupaca operation maintains ITAR registration through the DDTC.

Customers span aerospace, agriculture, defense, electrical, food processing, gas and oil, health care and medical equipment, power generation and distribution (including wind), power sports, marine, and data centers. The client base ranges from small businesses to Fortune 500 companies such as Eaton Corporation's Power Systems Division. Dielectric also distributes unfinished thermoplastics, thermosets, ferrous and non-ferrous metals, and carbon fiber composites in sheet, rod, tube, and block forms.

The company emphasizes a partner-oriented approach, offering material selection guidance and design-for-manufacturability input to reduce cost and lead time. Standard lead times are quoted at two weeks, with expedited turnaround demonstrated on urgent orders. ITAR compliance and ongoing CMMC 2.0 implementation support defense-sector work.
